text: Seabrook Town secured a 4-2 victory over Harbour City, with Kian Romano scoring twice in stoppage time to decisively turn the match in their favor [#1882] [#1906]. While Harbour City controlled possession with a patient short-passing style and created high-quality chances, exemplified by Elias Okafor's goal from a 17-pass sequence and Marek Barros's set-piece goal, the team's efforts were hampered by a red card to Joon Whitfield at 43 minutes, impacting their defensive stability [#904] [#905] [#973] [#975] [#871]. Seabrook Town's successful tactical shift around the 65th minute, increasing pressing intensity and directness, enabled aggressive high pressing and quicker attacks, leading to effective counters and four goals [#1361] [#1104]. This match highlights the critical importance of adapting pressing intensity and transition speed against possession-based teams. Coaching focus: train players to maintain defensive compactness and composure when reduced to ten men to minimize vulnerability during critical periods.

- Their tactical change around the 65th minute increased their pressing intensity (press from 0.66 to 0.84), directness (0.42 to 0.57), and line height (0.6 to 0.72), reflecting a shift to more aggressive high pressing and direct attacks to chase the game, consistent with their wide crossing and pressing style [#1361].
- Harbour City scored from a lengthy, patient build-up (17 passes over 56.9 seconds) culminating in a through ball assist from Marek Barros, fitting their 4-2-3-1 formation and patient short-passing style aiming to control possession and create high-quality chances [#904,905].
- Later, Marek Barros’s goal came from a corner-related scenario involving a cross, showing Harbour City’s use of set pieces to create scoring opportunities from a typically possession-focused formation [#973,975].

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals compared to Harbour City's 2, winning the match 4-2 [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].
- Kian Romano scored twice in stoppage time at 90+2' and 90+3', turning the game in Seabrook Town's favor [#1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros, player of the match, contributed with 1 goal, 2 assists, 4 tackles, 5 key passes, and 9 interceptions with a perfect rating of 10.0 [player_of_the_match].
- Seabrook Town had significantly higher xG at 3.53 vs Harbour City's 1.26, reflecting their superior attack [team_stats].
- Harbour City received a red card at 43' (Joon Whitfield), likely affecting their defensive capabilities [#871].
